doc.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024

title: Her father Sammy and singing in Woonsocket
summary: Prompted by a tune, she describes her trombonist father Sammy, his weekend band, her early singing and the songs he wrote out for her.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: He’s decomposing. Okay I want to take you back a bit and I’m going to do that by seeing if you can name this tune. All right? I’ll give it my best rendition. [scats]

[sings] “perhaps someone else may be nearer/your heart.” Interesting that you should do that one. It’s not one — it’s not necessarily a staple that I have played throughout, and I’m not even sure I can recall that many people asking for it, but it was a song that I sang a lot in my home in Woonsocket, Rhode Island, and I probably heard it on the radio or on the many recordings that my father would play. My father, Sammy, was a trombonist and although he was mainly working in our family restaurant, on the weekends he usually would have some kind of a steady weekend gig with his band and that was my first most important mentorship. And I was told I could sing before I could talk and there was — we didn’t have a real piano but there was some keyboard that he had that I started to fiddle with. But he then encouraged me when we got — and I used to call it a “junky upright” to play, this is probably even before I was taking lessons and he had — he always would write out some songs that he would play on his gigs. They were always standards, and he would write the melody line and chords, although the melody was © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
written in the trombone bass line. But I don’t think that was one of them. The one that I remember, and I never sing it it’s too rangy, is “I’ll Get By.”
[sings] “I’ll get by as long as I have you.” And I didn’t know anything from Billie Holiday at that time, but the songs I did, and “Once in a While” I sang it, I knew it, I liked it.
I don’t even remember, who do you like singing it? Because who had the big hit on it? I don’t even know.
